To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the binding of a protein containing a number of binding sites to an immobilized ligand containing multiple binding sites may be cooperative and (ii) the binding of the same protein to immobilized ligands containing multiple binding sites is accompanied by metastable adsorption states.
the binding of proteins with immobilized binding sites (e.g. receptors) on the surface of biomembranes is cooperative and is accompanied by metastable adsorption states.
The binding of proteins to surfaces with immobilized ligands (e.g., butyl agarose) and to cell membranes can be described by the Langmuir adsorption equation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interactions of proteins with immobilized binding sites, and the application of these studies to the analysis of biological processes.
the binding and regulation of proteins on cellular interfaces.
the binding of proteins on surfaces and with the interactions of proteins with surfaces containing multiple binding sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phosphorylase b adsorption is a cooperative, multivalent, and metastable process.
the adsorption of proteins on surfaces containing immobilized ligands can be described as a cooperative process.

the adsorption of phosphoryylase b on immobilized butyl groups is a complex process involving metastable states and that this process may be analyzed in terms of the binding of a multivalent protein to a multivalent surface containing a lattice of binding sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interactions of a protein with immobilized ligands are not simply related to those of the protein with soluble ligands.

we have demonstrated that proteins may be immobilized on agarose gels in a manner which allows them to be studied in a state of high activity and in a form which is easily separated from unbound protein and from other proteins.
the binding of proteins (e. g., enzymes) to immobilized ligands is a cooperative process which may be analyzed in terms of the thermodynamics of binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interactions of proteins with immobilized solutes (or receptors) on cell surfaces can be studied by model systems.
the interactions of proteins with cell surface receptors can be analyzed in terms of a binding isotherm which is analogous to the Langmuir adsorption isotherm.
protein binding to cell-surface structures is a complex process which can be analyzed in a systematic manner.
